# Proof that the Counit of Spectrum Adjunction is a Natural Transformation

Let $\mathbf{Frm}$ denote the category of frames and frame homomorphisms. The category of locales $\mathbf{Loc}$ is defined as the opposite category of frames, $\mathbf{Frm}^{op}$. For any locale $L$, let $\mathcal{O}(L)$ denote its corresponding frame. A locale morphism $f: L_1 \to L_2$ corresponds formally to a frame homomorphism, which we denote as $f^*: \mathcal{O}(L_2) \to \mathcal{O}(L_1)$.

Let $\mathbf{\Omega}: \mathbf{Top} \to \mathbf{Loc}$ be the locale of open sets functor. For any topological space $X$, $\mathbf{\Omega}(X)$ is the locale whose frame is the topology of $X$, denoted $\mathcal{O}(X)$. For a continuous map $g: X \to Y$, the morphism $\mathbf{\Omega}(g): \mathbf{\Omega}(X) \to \mathbf{\Omega}(Y)$ in $\mathbf{Loc}$ corresponds to the frame homomorphism $\mathbf{\Omega}(g)^* = g^{-1}: \mathcal{O}(Y) \to \mathcal{O}(X)$.

Let $\operatorname{Sp}: \mathbf{Loc} \to \mathbf{Top}$ be the spectrum functor. For any locale $L$, the spectrum $\operatorname{Sp}(L)$ is the topological space whose points are the frame homomorphisms $p: \mathcal{O}(L) \to \{0, 1\}$. The topology on $\operatorname{Sp}(L)$ is given by the open sets of the form $\Sigma_a = \{ p \in \operatorname{Sp}(L) \mid p(a) = 1 \}$ for each $a \in \mathcal{O}(L)$. For a locale morphism $f: L_1 \to L_2$, the continuous map $\operatorname{Sp}(f): \operatorname{Sp}(L_1) \to \operatorname{Sp}(L_2)$ is defined by mapping a point $p \in \operatorname{Sp}(L_1)$ to $p \circ f^* \in \operatorname{Sp}(L_2)$.

The counit of the adjunction $\mathbf{\Omega} \dashv \operatorname{Sp}$ is a family of locale morphisms $\sigma_L: \mathbf{\Omega}(\operatorname{Sp}(L)) \to L$ for each $L \in \mathbf{Loc}$. In the category $\mathbf{Frm}$, this corresponds to a frame homomorphism $\sigma_L^*: \mathcal{O}(L) \to \mathcal{O}(\mathbf{\Omega}(\operatorname{Sp}(L)))$. Since the open sets of $\operatorname{Sp}(L)$ are precisely the sets $\Sigma_a$, the frame $\mathcal{O}(\mathbf{\Omega}(\operatorname{Sp}(L)))$ is exactly $\{\Sigma_a \mid a \in \mathcal{O}(L)\}$. The homomorphism is given by $\sigma_L^*(a) = \Sigma_a$.

To prove that $\sigma: \mathbf{\Omega}\operatorname{Sp} \to \operatorname{id}_{\mathbf{Loc}}$ is a natural transformation, we must show that for any locale morphism $f: L_1 \to L_2$, the following diagram commutes in $\mathbf{Loc}$:
$$
\require{AMScd}
\begin{CD}
\mathbf{\Omega}(\operatorname{Sp}(L_1)) @>{\mathbf{\Omega}(\operatorname{Sp}(f))}>> \mathbf{\Omega}(\operatorname{Sp}(L_2)) \\
@V{\sigma_{L_1}}VV @VV{\sigma_{L_2}}V \\
L_1 @>>{f}> L_2
\end{CD}
$$
Equivalently, passing to the opposite category $\mathbf{Frm}$, we must show that the corresponding diagram of frame homomorphisms commutes:
$$
\require{AMScd}
\begin{CD}
\mathcal{O}(\mathbf{\Omega}(\operatorname{Sp}(L_1))) @<{\mathbf{\Omega}(\operatorname{Sp}(f))^*}<< \mathcal{O}(\mathbf{\Omega}(\operatorname{Sp}(L_2))) \\
@A{\sigma_{L_1}^*}AA @AA{\sigma_{L_2}^*}A \\
\mathcal{O}(L_1) @<<{f^*}< \mathcal{O}(L_2)
\end{CD}
$$
That is, we need to prove that $\sigma_{L_1}^* \circ f^* = \mathbf{\Omega}(\operatorname{Sp}(f))^* \circ \sigma_{L_2}^*$.

Let $b \in \mathcal{O}(L_2)$. Applying the right-hand composition to $b$, we have:
$$
(\mathbf{\Omega}(\operatorname{Sp}(f))^* \circ \sigma_{L_2}^*)(b) = \mathbf{\Omega}(\operatorname{Sp}(f))^*(\sigma_{L_2}^*(b)) = \mathbf{\Omega}(\operatorname{Sp}(f))^*(\Sigma_b)
$$
By the definition of the functor $\mathbf{\Omega}$ on morphisms, $\mathbf{\Omega}(\operatorname{Sp}(f))^*$ acts by taking the inverse image under the continuous map $\operatorname{Sp}(f)$. Thus:
$$
\mathbf{\Omega}(\operatorname{Sp}(f))^*(\Sigma_b) = (\operatorname{Sp}(f))^{-1}(\Sigma_b)
$$
Expanding the inverse image using the definition of $\operatorname{Sp}(f)$, we obtain:
$$
(\operatorname{Sp}(f))^{-1}(\Sigma_b) = \{ p \in \operatorname{Sp}(L_1) \mid \operatorname{Sp}(f)(p) \in \Sigma_b \}
$$
$$
= \{ p \in \operatorname{Sp}(L_1) \mid p \circ f^* \in \Sigma_b \}
$$
$$
= \{ p \in \operatorname{Sp}(L_1) \mid (p \circ f^*)(b) = 1 \}
$$
$$
= \{ p \in \operatorname{Sp}(L_1) \mid p(f^*(b)) = 1 \}
$$
$$
= \Sigma_{f^*(b)}
$$
Now, applying the left-hand composition to $b$, we have:
$$
(\sigma_{L_1}^* \circ f^*)(b) = \sigma_{L_1}^*(f^*(b)) = \Sigma_{f^*(b)}
$$
Since both compositions evaluate to $\Sigma_{f^*(b)}$ for an arbitrary element $b \in \mathcal{O}(L_2)$, the frame homomorphisms are equal. 

Therefore, the diagram commutes for all morphisms $f$, which proves that the counit $\sigma$ is a natural transformation. $\blacksquare$
